links.outcome: Performance variation by acquisition parameter (view type) across chest X-ray datasets
links.effect: View type accounted for 87% (RSNA) and 69% (NIH) of total observed performance range; PA-view miss rates 30-78%; OR for missed diagnosis 6.69 (RSNA) and 13.02 (NIH).
links.quote: All five models demonstrated systematic posteroanterior view underdiagnosis with miss rates of 30-78%.

links.outcome: Performance disparities across age, sex, and technical subgroups masked by aggregate metrics
links.effect: View type explained 69-87% of performance range, age 5-30%, sex under 2%; subgroup gaps not visible in aggregate performance.
links.quote: Age explained 5-30% of the total observed performance range depending on dataset, while sex consistently explained less than 2%.

unlisted_practices: Auditing AI performance across technical acquisition parameters (e.g., radiograph view type) alongside demographic subgroup analysis

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates five pre-trained chest X-ray models across multiple datasets to assess how technical acquisition parameters (view type) cause performance disparities relative to demographics. However, it does not test an organizational deployment practice or guardrail implementation directly.
